description: A creamy, rich, and mildly spiced chicken dish, Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani) is a beloved classic of Indian cuisine. Tender pieces of chicken are marinated, grilled or pan-fried, then simmered in a luscious tomato-based gravy infused with butter, cream, and aromatic spices. This iconic dish offers a harmonious blend of sweet, tangy, and savory flavors, making it a perfect comfort food experience.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice. Mix well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer (cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding). Cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 2 tablespoons of ghee or butter. Add green cardamom pods, cloves, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Saute for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Build the Gravy Flavor
instructions.text: Add ginger-garlic paste to the pan and cook for 1 minute until the raw smell disappears. Stir in tomato puree, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and garam masala. Cook, stirring frequently, for 8-10 minutes, until the mixture thickens and the oil separates from the sides.

instructions.title: Add Cashews and Simmer
instructions.text: Drain the soaked cashews and blend them with a little water until a smooth paste is formed. Add the cashew paste to the tomato mixture. Stir in sugar and salt to taste. Add water or chicken stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, and cloves (optional, for smoother gravy). For an extra smooth gravy, carefully blend the mixture using an immersion blender or transfer to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pan. Add the cooked chicken to the gravy. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed Kasuri Methi. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors and the gravy to thicken slightly. Do not boil vigorously after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice for a complete Indian meal.

tips: For an authentic smoky flavor, you can char the cooked chicken pieces slightly under a broiler or on a grill after cooking them in the pan, before adding them to the gravy.
Adjust the amount of red chili powder for your preferred spice level. For a richer color without too much heat, use Kashmiri red chili powder.

If you don't have Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves), you can omit it, but it adds a distinctive aroma and flavor that is characteristic of authentic Butter Chicken. Look for it in Indian grocery stores.
article:
Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani: A Timeless Indian Delight

The aroma of Indian spices wafting from a simmering pot is a universally comforting experience. Among the vast and diverse tapestry of Indian cuisine, one dish stands out as a global superstar: Butter Chicken, or as it's traditionally known, Murgh Makhani. This creamy, rich, and mildly spiced chicken dish has captured the hearts and palates of millions worldwide, becoming a staple in Indian restaurants and a beloved home-cooked meal. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality dish in your own kitchen, you've come to the right place. This article will guide you through mastering the classic Butter Chicken, ensuring a flavorful and authentic experience that will transport your taste buds straight to the streets of Delhi.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, translates literally to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, it's credited to the Moti Mahal restaurant. The dish was born from a desire to utilize leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato-based gravy. What emerged was a culinary masterpiece: tender pieces of marinated chicken, often grilled or pan-fried, bathed in a velvety sauce made from tomatoes, butter, cream, and a blend of aromatic spices. Its hallmark is a subtle sweetness balanced by a mild tang and a creamy texture that is utterly irresistible. Unlike many spicier Indian curries, Butter Chicken offers a gentle warmth, making it approachable for all palates, and it's this harmonious balance of flavors and luxurious mouthfeel that has cemented its status as an iconic dish. It’s more than just a meal; it’s a cultural ambassador for Indian cuisine, celebrated for its comforting richness and vibrant taste.

## Ingredients You Need for Butter Chicken

Crafting an exceptional Butter Chicken requires a careful selection of fresh ingredients. The beauty lies in the quality of each component, building layers of flavor.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Makhani (Butter) Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 (28 ounce) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 large fresh tomatoes, blanched, peeled, and pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews (soaked in hot water for 15 minutes, then drained)
*   1/2 cup water (plus more if needed)
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances acidity)
*   1 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Butter Chicken

Making Butter Chicken might seem daunting, but by breaking it down into manageable steps, you'll find it incredibly rewarding.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours for maximum flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large non-stick pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until browned and slightly charred, but not fully cooked through. Set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Add Spices and Tomatoes:** Reduce the heat to low. Stir in the red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, ground cumin, and ground coriander. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, to toast the spices. Be careful not to burn them. Immediately add the crushed tomatoes (or fresh tomato puree) and the soaked cashews.
5.  **Simmer and Blend:** Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the sauce has thickened slightly. Remove from heat and let it cool slightly. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender) and blend until completely smooth. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture, pressing down on solids to extract all liquid. This step is crucial for the classic smooth finish of Butter Chicken.
6.  **Combine and Finish:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Add 1/2 cup of water, sugar, and salt to taste. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender, absorbing the flavors of the sauce.
7.  **Final Touches:** Stir in the crushed fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). This spice adds a distinctive, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor essential to authentic Butter Chicken. Finally, swirl in the heavy cream and an extra knob of butter (if desired) for extra richness. Heat through gently, but do not boil after adding the cream, as it can curdle. Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken is within reach with a few expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don’t skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse it with flavor, making a huge difference in the final taste and texture. Overnight marination is ideal.
*   **Charred Chicken Adds Depth:** If possible, lightly char the marinated chicken under a broiler or on a grill before adding it to the sauce. The smoky flavor significantly enhances the complexity of the dish. If pan-frying, ensure good browning.
*   **Smooth Sauce is a Must:** Blending the sauce thoroughly and then straining it through a fine-mesh sieve is the secret to that characteristic silky-smooth texture. Don't skip this step!
*   **Kasoori Methi (Fenugreek Leaves):** This ingredient is non-negotiable for authentic Murgh Makhani flavor. Lightly crush the dried leaves between your palms before adding them to release their aromatic oils.
*   **Balance Sweetness and Acidity:** The sugar helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes. Taste and adjust to your preference. A little extra butter at the end can also round out the flavors beautifully.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

The rich and creamy nature of Murgh Makhani makes it incredibly versatile for pairing. The most classic accompaniment is warm, fluffy naan bread, perfect for scooping up every last drop of that delicious sauce. Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) also makes an excellent canvas for the curry. To cut through the richness, consider serving it with a simple side salad of sliced cucumbers and onions, or a cooling raita (yogurt dip) with cucumber and mint. A sprinkle of fresh cilantro not only adds a pop of color but also a fresh herbaceous note, making your Butter Chicken even more special.

## Variations and Substitutions for Butter Chicken

While the classic recipe is sublime, there are many ways to customize your Butter Chicken to suit dietary needs or personal preferences:

*   **Healthier Option:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or substitute heavy cream with a lighter alternative like half-and-half or even coconut milk for a dairy-free version.
*   **Dairy-Free/Vegan:** For a completely dairy-free version, use coconut oil instead of butter, and substitute heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream. For a vegan dish, replace chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), tofu, or even chickpeas and vegetables.
*   **Spicier Kick:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add a pinch of cayenne pepper to the sauce. A sliced green chili added during the simmering stage can also provide a fresh burst of heat.
*   **Protein Alternatives:** While chicken is traditional, you can make this recipe with paneer (Paneer Makhani), shrimp, or even lamb for a different take on the creamy sauce.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you don't have a broiler or grill, you can add a smoky flavor by placing a small piece of hot charcoal in a small metal bowl in the center of the finished curry, drizzling a teaspoon of ghee over it, and quickly covering the pot for a few minutes.

Bringing the magic of classic Butter Chicken to your home kitchen is a truly rewarding experience. With this comprehensive guide, you’re now equipped to create a dish that’s rich, flavorful, and incredibly satisfying. Enjoy the process, and savor every spoonful of this timeless Indian delicacy!
